summary.headline: BlueStone Q2 FY27 revenue grew 44% YoY to INR 738 crore, EBITDA more than doubled, and the company posted its fourth consecutive standalone profitable quarter.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 738 crore, up 44% YoY, with EBITDA more than doubling and a fourth straight profitable quarter on a standalone basis. Management said about 29% of the 44% growth came from AOV increase, with the rest from buyer growth, and that SSSG was around 28% in the quarter. The company crossed 1 million customers, opened 27 stores across 7 new cities, and reset entry-level price points, which lowered sequential AOV. Management said festive-season timing shifted some demand into Q3, and that early Q3 trends were in line with expectations, with most big buying days still ahead.

financial_highlights.change: YoY as stated, no figure given
Q2 FY27 as cited by analyst
Close to 30% AOV growth per analyst
Management expects about 4.5% in roughly four years
Below FY25 and FY26 levels per analyst

segments.name: Online and store retail
segments.commentary: Online is the primary acquisition channel with no BTL spend; stores opened 27 in the quarter across 7 new cities, mostly Tier-2 and Tier-3, with some in existing metros. Store count was about 340 in FY26, with the company targeting about 380 now and closer to 500 in coming months (per analyst).

guidance_outlook: Management expects further inventory turn improvement at the aggregate level as older cohorts mature and gold prices stabilise.
Management guided A&P spend to fall to around 4.5% of revenue over roughly the next four years.
Management reiterated a long-term revenue ambition of INR 12,000 crore by 2030 (per analyst question; not re-confirmed in management answer).
Management expects Q3 to show clearly whether buyer growth offsets slower AOV growth as gold prices stabilise.
Board gave in-principle approval for an INR 300 crore NCD raise, primarily to retire higher-cost debt; coupon and tenure not disclosed.
capex_capacity: Store expansion: 27 stores opened in Q2 FY27 across 7 new cities (mostly Tier-2 and Tier-3).
Flagship store at Park Street, Kolkata launched as an experiment; management may open one or two more, featuring handmade and Kundan products.
Design portfolio exceeds 10,500 designs; new handcrafted and antique range launched at Park Street.

Working capital: management said the IPO-raised INR 750 crore for working capital is exhausted (per analyst); funding now relies on internal accruals, low net debt-to-equity, and customer advances and schemes.
Inventory and store productivity: older cohorts (5 to 7 years) win more inventory only if they achieve 1.8 to 2 turns with continued growth.
demand_pricing: AOV fell sequentially as entry-level price points were reset; management said the AOV decline was intentional and is producing results.
Management said repeat customers buy at higher AOV than new customers, and that repeat is strong (rejecting an analyst's flattish-repeat characterisation).
Management said new-customer growth was weaker last year after gold rose 50-70%, and that entry price points were redesigned from Q3 FY26.
Festive timing: Navratri started late, so only 10-11 days of the season were visible at the time of the call; Karwa Chauth and Dhanteras are still ahead.
Lab-grown diamonds: management said consumers in stores are not asking for LGD; the company's solitaire share is under 1%, and LGD is taking share mainly from solitaires.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the SSSG was shifted into Q3 due to the festive timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to quantify the shift, but acknowledged a reasonable impact and gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: Can AOV growth continue if gold prices are flat, and what is the buyer growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth has not swung much with gold prices; about 10-15% ticket growth comes from repeat customers maturing, with buyer growth expected to contribute more as gold stays stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cohort data status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly cohort data, saying cohorts are better reviewed in blocks; some disclosure already exists.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Tier-3 expansion different in assortment and price points?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no meaningful price-point difference between Tier-1, 2 and 3 customers, and that marketing stays online with no BTL.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the 2030 INR 12,000 crore revenue target and the working capital need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding comes from internal accruals as stores mature, low net debt-to-equity, and third-party liabilities such as customer advances and schemes; it sees no funding challenge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 300 crore NCD for, and what is the coupon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an in-principle Board approval to retire higher-cost debt and lower blended cost of debt; coupon and tenure will be disclosed when finalised.

risks_watch: AOV growth normalises as gold prices stabilise; buyer growth must offset it in Q3.
Festive demand timing: part of Q2 demand shifted into Q3, and Q3 trends are not yet visible.
Contribution margin and studded mix: margin fell about 50 bps YoY while studded share declined; management declined to break down drivers.
Inventory: management gave no target inventory level or kilogram figure; GMROI on reported basis is lower than prior years, and management points to cohort vintage.
Financing: NCD terms unknown; the cost of debt reduction is not quantified.
Management declined to give cohort data quarterly, reducing visibility into vintage performance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, customer reach and margin health, but evasive on quantification: management declined to size festive shift, cohort data, contribution margin drivers, NCD terms and the cost reduction.
key_quotes: Revenue grew 44% year-on-year to INR 738 crores, EBITDA more than doubled, and this is our fourth consecutive profitable quarter on a standalone basis.
It took us 15 years to reach our first million customers. The next million will come much faster.
So, I think there is no point in giving cohort data every quarter, and there is no intention to do that, as well.

growth.why: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 44% YoY to INR 738 crore (about 29 points from AOV, rest from buyers), with 27 new stores across 7 cities and a 4.5% A&P target, but no explicit revenue guidance for the year; the INR 12,000 crore 2030 ambition was raised by an analyst and not reaffirmed by management.
